newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares renewed their downward move on Wednesday as sentiment took a triple knock from the ongoing bullion price fall, a shaky rand and a poorly performing bond market, dealers said.
The gold sector was the worse hit and a renewed drop in the price of the yellow metal to $317 an ounce saw Tuesday's mini-rally evaporate and local shares started to head downwards.
"Gold took a knock again. Some people were calling the bottom yesterday (Tuesday), but that looks to have been a little premature," one dealer said.
The gold index lost 18.4 points, or 1.99 percent, to end at 905.3 as Western Deep sheds 75 cents to 95.00 rand and Randgold drops 90 cents to 15.90 rand.
Analysts said gold will remain vulnerable with the start of the local gold mining industry's second quarter reporting season fast approaching and unlikely to provide much in the way of good news.
"I think we are going to see a bloodbath in general," Mathison and Hollidge gold analyst Angus Auchterlonie said.
Platinum stocks also came under pressure after the white metal price dipped below $400 amid bullion woes and fears that Russia may start exporting stocks later this year.
The platinum index closed off 139 points at 4,964.0 as Rusplats was down 175 cents to 74.50 rand, Lebowa Platinum fell 30 cents to 430 cents and Potgieterust Platinum slid 100 cents to 30.00 rand.
The metals market worries impacted on sentiment in industrials which were also hit by a poor local bond market and continued worries over the rand.
Some dealers also said there was still a perception that strong gains last month were in need of a further correction.

The rand hit a new five-month lows against the dollar on Wednesday after a flurry of offshore demand prompted a break of key resistance at 4.56, while the key R150 bond was last at 14.235 percent from Tuesday's 1507 GMT level of 14.10 pct.

The gloomy mood saw the all-share index drop 11.1 points to 7,299.2 as industrials dipped 7.0 points to 8,759.3, though an afternoon bout of futures-related buying prvided some strong support at lower levels and prompted a late rise.
Trade was brisk with 750 milion rands worth of shares changing hands and 202 shares dropped against 149 gainers.
Shares were seen drifting on Thursday with little strong movement either way, though golds will remain vulnerable to the bullion price.

Among gainers was Liberty Life which jumped 600 cents to end at 139.00 rand on positive market reaction to an investor roadshow and provided a boost for the financials index which added 57.3 points to 10,142.6 and the insurance index which put on 203 points to 11,314.8.
Shares in Multisource Holdings Ltd, which is to be reconstituted as a private investment firm, also rose strongly as investors welcomed the move and scrambled for limited stock
The firm ended up 25.0 percent, or 350 cents, to a new year high of 17.50 rand, making it the second biggest percentage gainer on the Johannesburg bourse.
In the futures market contracts recovered off their early lows and ended almost level.
Dealers said there was likely to be a touch more futures-related buying into spot on Thursday.
The all-share September contract was last at 6,627/40 from 6,680 settlement as the gold contract was at 636/48 from 652. The industrials contract was at 8,425/32 from 8,517.
-- Paul Harris, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
